about: Phase 6 statement-level audit of the Lean physics volumes (docs/research/CLAIM_TIGHTENING_ROADMAP.md). One row per physics-sounding theorem/lemma in lean_proofs/Vol*.lean, decided from the Phase 6 review (lean_proofs/check_statement_audit.py --review) and the module inventory in PROOF_AUDIT.md. Rows may carry a `previous_name` -- a name this pass retired; the gate checks that the retired name is a declaration nowhere and a live token nowhere.
method: Rows are judgements recorded per declaration, not machine-proved claims: a witness is checked to exist (and to differ from its theorem), a stated_condition to occur verbatim in the statement, a source to exist, and a previous_name to be absent from the corpus with comments masked. What the kernel can check is checked by CI's lake build ToE, which compiles every witness and source named here. `previous_name` is validated on any row, not only on `renamed` rows: a rename performed by a later pass lands under the new name and keeps its disposition.

dispositions.witness: the statement is about a declared, non-degenerate object or instance (named in `witness`); its hypotheses, where it has any, are realized
dispositions.conditional: the statement carries its hypotheses in its own signature (`stated_condition` quotes the text)
dispositions.renamed: the name was changed so it no longer overstates; `previous_name` is the retired name and must not survive anywhere
dispositions.carried: true only from data the model carries (structure field, postulate, placeholder or constant definition, definitional restatement, or degenerate instance), so no non-degenerate witness exists; `source` names the declaration that carries it

lexicon: The candidate census is lexical: a theorem/lemma counts when one of the words in its name (split on _, ., camelCase) is a PHYSICS_TOKENS word in check_statement_audit.py. The lexicon is a floor, not a ceiling.

rows.name: affine_poisson_antisymm
rows.note: Antisymmetry of the affine bracket: a polynomial identity on the declared definition.

rows.name: affine_poisson_jacobi
rows.note: Jacobi identity for the concrete affine-observable algebra; the docstring states it is a genuine polynomial identity, not an assumption.

rows.name: affine_poisson_self
rows.note: Alternation of the affine bracket on affine observables; the bracket is the concrete polynomial definition.

rows.name: conservation_of_energy
rows.note: H(t₁) = H(t₂) for all times under the stated differentiability hypotheses; conservation is derived, not assumed.
rows.stated_condition: hV : ∀ x, HasDerivAt V (V' x) x

rows.name: constant_commutator_eval_at_zero
rows.note: In the constant-evaluation helper `lim_h_to_0 f := f 0`, evaluating the constant family `fun _ => commutator A B` returns `{A, B}` by rfl; the non-constant Weyl scaling correspondence is `weyl_commutator_quotient_eq_poisson`. Renamed from `commutator_limit`.

rows.name: energy_deriv_zero
rows.note: dH/dt = 0 along any differentiable solution of q̇ = p/m, ṗ = −V′(q); the differentiability hypotheses are in the signature.
rows.stated_condition: hq : ∀ t, HasDerivAt q (p t / m) t

rows.name: force_eq_mass_times_accel
rows.note: Newton's second law as uniqueness of the derivative of m*v: the two differentiability hypotheses are stated, so nothing beyond F = d(mv)/dt is assumed.
rows.stated_condition: hF : HasDerivAt (fun s => m * v s) F t

rows.name: linear_map_scales_omega
rows.note: A 2×2 linear map scales the planar symplectic 2-form `omega` by its determinant `ad - bc`: polynomial identity on the concrete bilinear form.

rows.name: mass_emergence
rows.note: The 'mass' is the declared state-norm-squared invariant ‖ρ‖², and the theorem states its nonnegativity as an existential. Strict positivity on nonzero states is `modular_spectrum_pos_of_ne_zero`; no emergence dynamics is claimed.

rows.name: omega_add_left
rows.note: Left additivity of the planar symplectic 2-form `omega X Y = X.1 * Y.2 - X.2 * Y.1`; ring algebra on the concrete definition.

rows.name: omega_antisymm
rows.note: Alternating sign `omega X Y = -omega Y X` of the declared planar symplectic 2-form.

rows.name: omega_coordinates
rows.note: Pairing with the canonical basis vectors `(0, 1)` and `(1, 0)` recovers `(X.1, -X.2)`, establishing coordinate recovery for `omega`.

rows.name: omega_nondegenerate
rows.note: Non-degeneracy of the planar symplectic form: if `omega X Y = 0` for all `Y`, evaluating at the basis vectors forces `X = 0`.

rows.name: omega_self
rows.note: Self-pairing `omega X X = 0` of the planar symplectic 2-form.

rows.name: omega_smul_left
rows.note: Left scalar homogeneity of the planar symplectic 2-form `omega`.

rows.name: poisson_antisymm
rows.note: Antisymmetry of the declared bracket {f,g} = ∂_q f ∂_p g − ∂_p f ∂_q g on ℝ×ℝ; ring algebra on the concrete definition, no hypotheses.

rows.name: poisson_canonical
rows.note: {q,p} = 1 on the canonical pair: the declared bracket is non-degenerate there, so the model is not a zero bracket.

rows.name: poisson_self
rows.note: {f,f} = 0 for the declared bracket; ring algebra on the concrete definition.

rows.name: symplectic_linear_map
rows.note: Symplectic-form (area) preservation by a linear map, conditional on determinant 1: the two-dimensional Liouville case.

rows.name: time_independent_hamiltonian_conserved
rows.note: A time-independent Hamiltonian with vanishing derivative is constant; the hypothesis is stated rather than hidden in a definition.

rows.name: uniform_gravity_force
rows.note: Uniform gravity as the constant-acceleration special case of F = d(mv)/dt; the trajectory derivative is the stated hypothesis.

rows.name: weyl_commutator_quotient_eq_poisson
rows.note: Exact Weyl correspondence on the affine algebra: [A,B]/iℏ = {A,B}; the division by ℏ is the stated hypothesis.

rows.name: field_strength_gauge_invariant
rows.note: d(A + dχ) = dA for smooth forms: gauge invariance of the field strength derived from d² = 0, with the smoothness hypotheses stated.

rows.name: gauge_transform_comp
rows.note: Gauge transformations compose additively on smooth form data: (A+dχ)+dψ = A+d(χ+ψ).

rows.name: maxwell_equations_of_sourced_field
rows.note: Conjunction of the homogeneous identity `d (d A) = 0` (from `d² = 0`) with the model law `law_dual_maxwell` carried by the sourced configuration, so only one conjunct is derived. Renamed from `maxwells_equations` in the Phase 6 rename pass.

rows.name: photonMass_eq_zero
rows.note: Definitional restatement (rfl) of the model postulate `PhotonMass := 0`; the docstring says it is not a derived result, so the name records the model's choice, not a derivation of photon masslessness. Renamed from `photon_massless` in the Phase 6 rename pass: the new name states the definition it unfolds.

rows.name: bh_entropy_pos
rows.note: Positivity follows from the carried area law `law_bekenstein_hawking : entropy = horizonArea / 4` and the field `area_pos`; the area law is a postulate of the structure, not derived.

rows.name: carnot_efficiency_lt_one
rows.note: η_Carnot = 1 − T_C/T_H < 1 for engines with 0 < T_C < T_H; `idealCarnotEngine` is the declared non-degenerate instance of that constraint set.

rows.name: carnot_efficiency_pos
rows.note: 0 < η_Carnot for the same constraint set, derived from the engine's temperature-order fields; the declared instance realizes it.

rows.name: clausius_equality_iff_reversible
rows.note: The iff is the carried balance law read at zero irreversibility: `irreversibility = 0` is what the structure calls reversible, so 'attainment' is definitional on the data.

rows.name: clausius_inequality
rows.note: ΔS ≥ Q/T is the carried fields `law_entropy_balance` and `irr_nonneg` unfolded; the docstring records that the hypotheses are satisfiable (T = 1, σ = 0).

rows.name: clausius_reversible_equality
rows.note: `heatExchange` is *defined* as T·ΔS, so ΔS = Q/T is arithmetic once the temperature is positive: reversibility is built into the definition.

rows.name: gibbsPartition_pos
rows.note: Z(β) = 1 + e^(−βΔE) > 0 for the declared partition function: genuine real analysis (exp_pos), no hypotheses.

rows.name: gibbsState_not_tracial
rows.note: ω_β(E₀₁E₁₀) ≠ ω_β(E₁₀E₀₁) for ΔE > 0, β ≠ 0: the two-level Gibbs state is non-tracial, the non-degenerate counterpart of the tracial model.

rows.name: gibbsState_one
rows.note: Normalization ω_β(1) = 1 of the declared Gibbs state; algebra on the definition with the partition function positive.

rows.name: heatExchange_nonneg_of_entropy_growth
rows.note: Q = T·ΔS ≥ 0 given entropy growth and a positive temperature: growth is the stated hypothesis, temperature positivity a structure field.

rows.name: idealCarnotEngine_attains_carnot
rows.note: The engine's `workOutput` is defined as (1 − T_C/T_H)·Q_in, so 'attaining Carnot efficiency' is true by construction; the docstring's 'benchmark' wording is the honest reading.

rows.name: kms_holds_at_every_temperature
rows.note: The tracial model is KMS at every β because its modular flow is the identity: the KMS equation is the trace equation ω_ρ_trace. Temperature content is degenerate; the non-degenerate two-level model is `twoLevel_kms_iff_eq`.

rows.name: kms_temperature_uniqueness_fails
rows.note: Refutation of the zeroth-law uniqueness premise in the tracial model, witnessed by KMS-at-every-β; this is why downstream statements carry temperature as data (`InEquilibrium`).

rows.name: twoLevel_kms_holds
rows.note: The two-level Gibbs state satisfies KMS at γ = β: the non-degenerate KMS model, proved by explicit modular algebra.

rows.name: twoLevel_kms_iff_eq
rows.note: KMS-temperature uniqueness in the non-tracial model: IsTwoLevelKMS ΔE β γ ↔ γ = β for a positive gap; the gap hypothesis is stated.

rows.name: twoLevel_kms_zeroth_law
rows.note: Two reservoirs KMS against one probe state have equal inverse temperature, conditional on the two KMS hypotheses and ΔE > 0.

rows.name: hamiltonian_self_adjoint
rows.note: Self-adjointness ⟨Hψ,φ⟩ = ⟨ψ,Hφ⟩ of the declared one-dimensional Hamiltonian for real energies: a concrete model operator.

rows.name: hasDerivAt_schrodingerTrajectory
rows.note: The declared trajectory ψ(t) = e^(−iωt)ψ₀ is differentiable with ψ′ = −iωψ: a genuine derivative, explicitly computed.

rows.name: robertson_uncertainty
rows.note: Var(A)·Var(B) ≥ (|⟨ψ,[A,B]ψ⟩|/2)² for self-adjoint A, B and a normalized ψ; the normalization (and self-adjointness) are stated hypotheses.

rows.name: schrodinger_equation
rows.note: iℏψ′ = H_{ℏω}ψ for the explicit trajectory and the declared Hamiltonian; the docstring notes the identity is proved without unfolding ℏ.

rows.name: horizonRadius_pos
rows.note: r_s = 2GM > 0 for positive mass (a structure field) given the stated G > 0.

rows.name: kretschmann_pos
rows.note: K = 48G²M²/r⁶ > 0 outside the horizon, conditional on G > 0 and r > 0.

rows.name: real_conservation_of_energy_momentum
rows.note: Derivative-level conservation: from the stated EFE relation and the contracted Bianchi identity, ∇·T = 0 for arbitrary coordinate tensor fields; genuine algebra with conditions stated.
rows.stated_condition: hEFE : ∀ μ α, G μ α = (8 * Real.pi * NewtonG) * T μ α

rows.name: unitSchwarzschild_horizon
rows.note: r_s = 2 for the unit benchmark (G = M = 1): a concrete, non-degenerate instance of the geometry.

rows.name: unitSchwarzschild_kretschmann_at_horizon
rows.note: K = 3/4 at the unit benchmark's horizon: an explicit nonzero value at a concrete instance.

rows.name: zeroCurvature_bianchi_identity
rows.note: ∇·G^μν = 0 for the zero Einstein tensor: the carried law field `law_bianchi_identity` read at the zero-curvature instance. Renamed from `bianchi_identity` in the Phase 6 rename pass: the qualifier names the degenerate instance.

rows.name: zeroCurvature_conservation_of_energy_momentum
rows.note: The statement is the zero-curvature instance's law: `stress_energy := 0`, so ∇·0 = 0. The name must not be read as a derived conservation law; this instance is deliberately degenerate. Renamed from `conservation_of_energy_momentum` in the Phase 6 rename pass: the qualifier names the degenerate instance the theorem is about.

rows.name: zeroCurvature_cosmological_constant
rows.note: An ∃Λ restatement of the instance's carried field `law_cosmological_constant` (Λ = 0 at the zero-curvature instance); a MODEL CLAIM by the docstring's own label. Renamed from `cosmological_constant` in the Phase 6 rename pass: the qualifier names the degenerate instance the theorem is about.

rows.name: zeroCurvature_einstein_field_equations
rows.note: G_μν = 8πG T_μν is the instance's carried law field `law_einstein_equations` with both sides 0 here; not a derivation of the field equations. Renamed from `einstein_field_equations` in the Phase 6 rename pass: the qualifier names the degenerate instance.

rows.name: zeroCurvature_metric_eq_qfim
rows.note: Both sides are 0 by definition at the zero-curvature instance (`metric := 0`; the model QFIM reduces definitionally), so this restates the instance's carried law field `law_metric_is_qfim`; the general claim is that field, not this theorem. Renamed from `metric_is_qfim` in the Phase 6 rename pass: the qualifier names the degenerate instance the theorem is about.

rows.name: zeroCurvature_stress_energy_eq_em_stress_energy
rows.note: `EMStressEnergy` is defined as `stress_energy`, so the identity is a definitional alias on the zero instance; no coupling between electromagnetism and gravity is established. Renamed from `em_sources_gravity` in the Phase 6 rename pass: the new name states the definitional alias instead of a gravity source.

rows.name: GaugeSymmetry_eq_product
rows.note: `GaugeSymmetry` is defined as SU3 × SU2 × U1, so this is the definition restated (rfl); no Lie-group structure is constructed. Renamed from `standard_model_gauge_group` in the Phase 6 rename pass: the new name states the definitional equality, not a gauge-group construction.

rows.name: diracOperator_eq_smul
rows.note: `DiracOperator ψ` is defined as `(DiracMass : ℂ) * ψ` with `DiracMass := 0`, so this is a definitional unfolding (rfl) and not a differential spinor equation. Renamed from `dirac_equation`.

rows.name: local_nets_isotony
rows.note: Interval inclusion `subset_region O₁ O₂` (`O₂.x_min ≤ O₁.x_min ∧ O₁.x_max ≤ O₂.x_max`) implies `LocalNet O₁ ⊆ LocalNet O₂` for the interval-supported operator family `LocalNet`.

rows.name: local_nets_microcausality
rows.note: On the 1D commutative carrier `OmegaAlgebra`, operator multiplication is commutative everywhere (`omegaAlgebra_commutative`); actual interval disjointness under spacelike separation is `local_nets_spacelike_disjoint`.

rows.name: local_nets_spacelike_disjoint
rows.note: Under `spacelike_separated O₁ O₂`, any support coordinates `x₁ ∈ [O₁.x_min, O₁.x_max]` and `x₂ ∈ [O₂.x_min, O₂.x_max]` are strictly distinct (`x₁ ≠ x₂`).

rows.name: nested_microcausality
rows.note: Composes `spacelike_hereditary` (genuine interval disjointness) with `local_nets_microcausality`, whose commutation conclusion is carried by the commutativity of `OmegaAlgebra`.

rows.name: placeholder_optical_expansion
rows.note: In the placeholder layer `SMatrix := 1` and `TMatrix := 0`, so the expansion is 1 = 1 by simp; the file keeps a separate hypothesis-carrying `placeholder_optical_theorem` wrapper, and no optical theorem is derived. Renamed from `optical_expansion` in the Phase 6 rename pass: the new name names the placeholder layer that makes it true.

rows.name: placeholder_optical_theorem
rows.note: Hypothesis-carrying wrapper around `placeholder_optical_expansion` at the same placeholder layer (`SMatrix := 1`, `TMatrix := 0`). Renamed from `optical_theorem`.

rows.name: regionA_B_spacelike
rows.note: Concrete disjoint intervals `regionA = [0, 1]` and `regionB = [2, 3]` witness `spacelike_separated regionA regionB`.

rows.name: spacelike_hereditary
rows.note: Sub-intervals of spacelike-separated intervals remain spacelike-separated (`subset_region O₁ O₂ ∧ subset_region O₃ O₄ ∧ spacelike_separated O₂ O₄ → spacelike_separated O₁ O₃`).

rows.name: constantScale_critical_density
rows.note: In the constant-scale-factor layer both `EnergyDensity` and `CriticalDensity` evaluate to 0; the parameterized non-degenerate equivalence is `FLRWUniverse.flat_friedmann_critical_density_eq`. Renamed from `criticaldensity`.

rows.name: constantScale_friedmann_equation
rows.note: In the constant-scale-factor layer (`ScaleFactor _ := 1`, `TimeDerivative _ _ := 0`, `EnergyDensity _ := 0`), both sides of the first Friedmann equation are 0 by simp. Renamed from `friedmannequations`.

rows.name: cosmological_redshift_ratio
rows.note: Ring rearrangement `1 + Redshift t_emit t_obs = ScaleFactor t_obs / ScaleFactor t_emit` of the `Redshift` definition; positivity under expansion is `FLRWUniverse.redshift_positive_of_expansion`. Renamed from `cosmologicalredshift`.

rows.name: criticalDensity_pos
rows.note: ρ_c = 3H²/(8πG) > 0 for the stated G > 0, with the rate positivity carried by the model.

rows.name: flat_friedmann_critical_density_eq
rows.note: H² = (8πG/3)ρ ↔ ρ = ρ_c: the flatness condition and the critical-density identity are the same algebraic relation, an equivalence under G > 0.

rows.name: redshift_positive_of_expansion
rows.note: z = a_obs/a_emit − 1 > 0 whenever the scale factor grows, with both factors positive as stated.

rows.name: bekenstein_hawking_entropy_def
rows.note: Definitional unfolding (rfl) of `BHEntropy bh := bh.horizonArea / (4 * NewtonG)`. Renamed from `bekensteinhawkingentropy`.

rows.name: bekenstein_hawking_entropy_pos
rows.note: `0 < BHEntropy bh` from `bh.area_pos` and `0 < NewtonG`, realized concretely by `standardSchwarzschild` (where `BHEntropy = 4π`). Renamed from `bhentropy_pos`.

rows.name: hawking_temperature_def
rows.note: Definitional unfolding (rfl) of `HawkingTemperature bh := bh.surfaceGravity / (2 * Real.pi)`. Renamed from `hawkingtemperature`.

rows.name: hawking_temperature_pos
rows.note: `0 < HawkingTemperature bh` from `bh.gravity_pos` and `0 < 2π`, realized concretely by `standardSchwarzschild` (where `T_H = 1/(8π)`). Renamed from `hawkingtemperature_pos`.

rows.name: kms_beta_hawking
rows.note: T_H is defined as κ/2π, so (2π/κ)·T_H = 1 is definitional arithmetic (κ > 0 is a structure field): it pins the definition, not a derivation of the Hawking temperature.

rows.name: kms_exterior_vacuum
rows.note: The exterior region's KMS state comes from the tracial model (identity modular flow, trace equation), so β is not pinned by the statement; the docstring points to `kms_beta_hawking` (definitional) and to the failure of temperature uniqueness.

rows.name: standardSchwarzschild_entropy
rows.note: S = A/4 = 4π on the unit-mass benchmark: a concrete value at a non-degenerate instance.

rows.name: standardSchwarzschild_hawking_temp
rows.note: T_H = κ/2π = 1/(8π) on the unit benchmark, whose surface gravity is nonzero.

rows.name: bell_correlation_det
rows.note: Explicit determinant `c₀₀ c₁₁ - c₀₁ c₁₀ = 1` on the declared two-qubit `bellState` witness.

rows.name: bell_entangled
rows.note: The declared `bellState` is non-separable (`Entangled bellState`), proved from its nonvanishing correlation determinant.

rows.name: bell_er_bridge
rows.note: The declared `bellState` satisfies `EinsteinRosenBridge bellState` (`correlationDet ≠ 0`).

rows.name: bell_er_epr
rows.note: Joint realization of `EinsteinRosenBridge` and `EPR_Entanglement` on the concrete `bellState` witness.

rows.name: bridge_entanglement_entropy_eq_bh_entropy
rows.note: `EntanglementEntropy` and `BHEntropy` are the same expression (`MinimalSurfaceArea`/4G), so the identity is definitional (dsimp); NOT a derivation of the holographic dictionary, as the docstring says. Renamed from `bridge_bh_entropy_is_holographic` in the Phase 6 rename pass: the new name states the identity, not a holographic dictionary.

rows.name: bulkFields_eq_boundaryFields_map
rows.note: `BulkFields p` is defined as `BoundaryFields (boundary_map p)` in the zero-field layer, so this is a definitional unfolding (rfl), not HKLL bulk reconstruction. Renamed from `bulk_reconstruction`.

rows.name: entanglementEntropy_eq_minimalSurfaceArea_div
rows.note: `EntanglementEntropy bh` is defined as `MinimalSurfaceArea bh / (4 * NewtonG)`, so this is a definitional unfolding (rfl), not a derivation of the Ryu-Takayanagi formula. Renamed from `ryu_takayanagi`.

rows.name: er_epr_bridge_entails_entanglement
rows.note: The sound direction of the ER=EPR dictionary in the two-qubit separability model, conditional on the bridge predicate; the converse is `product_of_correlation_det_zero` / `er_epr_iff`.

rows.name: er_epr_iff
rows.note: In the 2×2 two-qubit amplitude model, `EinsteinRosenBridge ψ ↔ EPR_Entanglement ψ` (nonzero determinant iff non-factorizable), realized by `bellState` and `productZeroState`.

rows.name: SM_Gauge_Group_eq_product
rows.note: `SM_Gauge_Group` is defined as SU3 × SU2 × U1, so this is the definition restated (rfl); the docstring says it is not a construction of Lie groups. Renamed from `gauge_symmetry` in the Phase 6 rename pass: the new name states the definitional equality, not a gauge-group construction.

rows.name: higgs_bounded_below
rows.note: `HiggsPotential φ = (φ² - v²)² ≥ 0` by `sq_nonneg` for every real amplitude `φ`.

rows.name: higgs_global_minimizers
rows.note: Global minimizers of the real quartic potential `HiggsPotential` are exactly `±VacuumExpectationValue`.

rows.name: higgs_vacuum_minimum
rows.note: V(φ) = (φ² − v²)² with v := 1, so V(v) = 0 is ring arithmetic on the definition; uniqueness of the minimizer needs a domain restriction (`higgs_zero_iff_nonneg`).

rows.name: higgs_zero_iff
rows.note: `HiggsPotential φ = 0 ↔ φ = v ∨ φ = -v` on the signed scalar amplitude model.

rows.name: higgs_zero_iff_nonneg
rows.note: Under the domain restriction `0 ≤ φ`, the unique zero of `HiggsPotential` is `φ = VacuumExpectationValue`.

rows.name: numberOfGenerations_eq_three
rows.note: Definitional restatement (rfl) of the stipulated constant `NumberOfGenerations := 3`; no generation count is derived. Renamed from `fermiongenerations`.

rows.name: chern_number_quantized
rows.note: Integrality of `b.chernNumber` for `ChernBand` (whose `chernIndex : ℤ` is a structure field), realized by `haldaneBand` (`C = 1`).

rows.name: chern_number_quantized_legacy
rows.note: In the legacy zero-Chern layer (`ChernNumber := 0`), integrality is witnessed by `0 : ℤ`.

rows.name: haldane_chern_number
rows.note: `haldaneBand.chernNumber = 1` on the concrete `C = 1` Chern-band benchmark.

rows.name: haldane_hall_conductance
rows.note: `haldaneBand.hallConductance e h = e² / h` on the concrete `C = 1` benchmark.

rows.name: hall_conductance_quantized
rows.note: Hall conductance is an integer multiple of `e² / h` for any `ChernBand`, realized with `n = 1` by `haldaneBand`.

rows.name: hall_conductance_quantized_legacy
rows.note: In the legacy zero-Chern layer (`ChernNumber := 0`), `HallConductance e h = 0 * (e² / h)`.

rows.name: landau_completed_square
rows.note: Completing the square on `LandauFreeEnergy a b T Tc m` under a strictly positive quartic coefficient `0 < b`.

rows.name: landau_critical_point_bounded
rows.note: At `T = Tc`, `LandauFreeEnergy a b Tc Tc m ≥ 0` whenever `b ≥ 0`.

rows.name: landau_critical_point_min
rows.note: `LandauFreeEnergy a b Tc Tc 0 = 0` by polynomial evaluation at `m = 0`.

rows.name: landau_critical_zero_iff
rows.note: At criticality `T = Tc` with `0 < b`, `LandauFreeEnergy a b Tc Tc m = 0 ↔ m = 0`.

rows.name: landau_flat_at_zero_quartic
rows.note: Boundary counterexample: at `b = 0` and `T = Tc`, `LandauFreeEnergy a 0 Tc Tc m = 0` for all `m`, showing `b > 0` is needed for uniqueness.

rows.name: landau_global_lower_bound
rows.note: Global lower bound `-(a(T - Tc))² / (4b) ≤ LandauFreeEnergy a b T Tc m` for `0 < b`.

rows.name: landau_lower_bound_attained
rows.note: When `0 < b` and `a * (T - Tc) ≤ 0`, both signed square-root branches attain the global lower bound.

rows.name: landau_lower_bound_eq_iff
rows.note: Equality with the completed-square lower bound holds iff `m² = -a(T - Tc) / (2b)`, conditional on `0 < b`.

rows.name: landau_minimizer_iff
rows.note: Complete characterization of global minimizers of `LandauFreeEnergy` in the ordered regime `a * (T - Tc) ≤ 0`, `0 < b`.

rows.name: bellPair_capacity
rows.note: `bellPairSystem.capacity = 2 * Real.log 2` on the declared 2-qubit Bell-pair benchmark.

rows.name: bellPair_strictly_below_capacity
rows.note: Single-subsystem entropy `ln 2` is strictly below the 2-qubit capacity `2 ln 2` on `bellPairSystem`.

rows.name: bellPair_subsystem_entropy
rows.note: S = ln 2 for the declared 2-qubit Bell benchmark, below its capacity 2 ln 2: a concrete non-degenerate instance.

rows.name: quantum_information_bound
rows.note: The bound is the structure's own field `h_bound` with capacity := n·ln 2; the declaration returns the carried constraint, it does not prove that nature honours it.

rows.name: bridge_vol13_entropy_nonneg
rows.note: Entropy nonnegativity restated for the Vol13 layer; the content is the QRegion fact (structure field `entropy_pos`).

rows.name: bridge_vol13_metric_self_zero
rows.note: Vol13's coupling fact `SM_Interaction g s` reduces to the model's self-distance identity; the wrapper certifies naming coherence, not a physical graviton coupling.

rows.name: sm_interaction_of_self_distance_zero
rows.note: `SM_Interaction` is defined as `∀ R, d R R = 0`, so it holds by `bridge_qregion_self_distance_zero`; no physical graviton coupling is derived. Renamed from `graviton_sm_coupling`.

rows.name: wheeler_dewitt_balance
rows.note: If `(H_m + H_g) Ψ = 0` on a state `Ψ`, then `H_m Ψ = -H_g Ψ`: additive-group algebra with the constraint stated as an explicit hypothesis.

rows.name: dark_energy_eq
rows.note: In any flat budget Ω_DE = 1 − Ω_b − Ω_dm; `standardLCDM` (0.05, 0.26, 0.69) is the declared non-degenerate instance.

rows.name: dark_energy_le_one
